title: Beyond Consensus | Overlooked Fundamentals and Market Blind Spots
summary: When market consensus concentrates on one direction, how do you systematically examine the fundamental changes consensus has obscured? Four cases — energy storage, non-ferrous metals, innovative pharma, and non-bank financials — build a cross-dimensional cross-validation research framework.

title: Case Study 01: Is Supply Still Driving the AI Cycle?
summary: Applying the Three-Layer Signal framework to the AI industry: supply signals remain tight, capital signals are accelerating expansion, and earnings signals are improving but not yet mature. Currently in the transition from investment phase to delivery phase.

title: The Blind Spot in Every Framework | Why Correct Analysis Doesn't Always Produce Correct Judgment
summary: Frameworks tell you what to look at, but they cannot guarantee that what you see is real. Three cognitive biases — availability bias, confirmation bias, and herding — can distort the input, execution, and output of analytical frameworks.

title: A Framework for Studying Technology Revolutions
summary: From supply constraints to commercial deployment: building a research framework for studying technology revolutions, using the AI industry as a case study. Find supply constraints, observe capital investment, wait for earnings delivery.

title: Three Forces Behind K-Shaped Divergence
summary: K-shaped divergence is not a random fluctuation. It is the result of three long-term economic forces working together: supply constraints in the AI industry, transformation of the macro policy framework, and restructuring of the global industrial division of labor.

title: When Historical Patterns Break: What We Really Need to Reconstruct
summary: What changes is statistical regularity; what remains constant is the logic of earnings-driven patterns. AI supply rigidity, misaligned capital structure, and policy framework shifts have together triggered a fundamental restructuring of the market.
